issues: Management/risk-register content is generally well used, but several mitigation-action statements read like confirmed, operating controls rather than ‘actions recorded in the register’, creating over-claim risk.
One risk-register numeric example is framed with an ‘estimated potential’ qualifier that is not evidenced as the register’s defined measure.
Some governance/control phrasing implies a more formalised ERM linkage and governance-control system than is evidenced (beyond the ERM-integration flag and semi-annual reporting).
available_evidence_omitted: 2024 governance alignment flags (TCFD aligned = true; IFRS S2 aligned = true) are not explicitly stated as indicators in the final boundaries subsection (draft states them, but not clearly as indicator flags and includes an over-strong implication elsewhere).
unsupported_claims: “ERM integration indicators show that climate-related risks are linked to the Bank’s enterprise risk management processes for a subset of recorded risks.” (partly supported by ERM-integration flags, but ‘linked to ERM processes’ is stronger than evidenced)

“Governance arrangements support the oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities described in the strategy, risk management and metrics and targets sections…” (generic linkage; not directly evidenced in the compact governance evidence)
material_unsupported_claims: Risk register example: “...associated with an estimated potential financial impact of EUR 165.2 million.” Evidence supports EUR 165.2 million, but the draft labels it “estimated potential financial impact” without confirming the register uses that exact definition; should be stated neutrally as “financial impact of EUR 165.2 million (as recorded in the register)” or similar.

Mitigation actions list includes items that are evidenced as labels in the register, but the draft presents them as implemented controls (e.g., “engagement and transition-plan covenants with borrowers”, “sector exposure limits and enhanced due diligence”). Without additional control-design/operating-effectiveness evidence, these should be framed as “recorded mitigation actions” rather than implying they are fully implemented bank-wide controls.

Overview: “climate checks for major transactions” is supported as an activity indicator, but the surrounding phrasing implies a more formalised control framework (“ERM integration indicators”, “climate checks”, “risk register” presented as a cohesive governance-control system). Needs tightening to avoid implying a formal control system beyond what is evidenced.

minor_wording_to_tighten: “These indicators show that climate-related matters were regularly considered at Board level.” (reasonable inference from agenda coverage; could be softened to “indicate”)

“The committee’s role in climate-related oversight is therefore described on the basis of its meeting frequency and recorded climate-related agenda coverage.” (acceptable, but could be simplified to avoid sounding methodological)

“The Bank operates a skills development programme that includes climate-related topics.” (supported as programme existence; could clarify it is a programme including climate topics, without implying breadth/mandatory coverage)
correctly_disclosed_evidence_boundaries: “The Bank does not disclose a separate ESG & Sustainability Committee charter or terms of reference in this report.”
“The Bank does not currently describe a separate formal process for assessing the adequacy of Board climate skills in this report.”
“ERM integration indicators show that 6 of 8 recorded climate-related risks carry an ERM-integration flag; enterprise-wide integration into the enterprise risk management framework is not evidenced.”
“Formal escalation thresholds or trigger-based escalation mechanics are not evidenced in the climate risk register.”
“Board decision evidence identifies climate-related decisions but does not describe quantified or specific Board-level trade-offs…”
Assurance boundary: limited assurance by EY under ISAE 3000 over Scope 1 and Scope 2 only; financed emissions and other Scope 3 outside scope.
